+//! "Pass starts at" for the planar Adaptive pocket (#3355): how the HSM
+//! plan honours the shared `PassStart` of #3316. Provenance: our own law
+//! from general machining practice (an adaptive cut starts from open
+//! air or grows from its own bore, never with a full-width slot along a
+//! wall) and the air-side plan of #1950 (Held 1991); no vendor material
+//! consulted.
+
+use crate::geo2d::Region;
+
+use super::face::GenError;
+use super::adaptive_method::AdaptiveMethod;
+use super::pass_start::PassStart;
+use super::pocket::{PocketParams, PocketStrategy, plan_passes_from};
+use super::pocket_hsm::{Planned, RINGS_FALLBACK, adaptive_ordered};
+
+/// The Adaptive pocket's passes under `start`. `stock` is the stock
+/// outline in the area's own frame (`None`: not known here).
+///
+/// - Auto: [`super::pocket_hsm::adaptive_passes`] with no stock, the plan
+///   every earlier file cut, byte for byte.
+/// - Outside: each piece is cut from the air past the stock edge inward
+///   and ends on its holes' walls (the #1950 air plan). Where a piece
+///   has no air side, the Offset rings cut the area from its outer
+///   boundary in, and the note says why.
+/// - Inside: an area without holes is the growth plan itself - it
+///   starts at its bore in the core and walks out to the outer wall. An
+///   area with holes cannot start on a hole wall without a full-width
+///   slot, so the Offset rings cut it from its holes out, said.
+///
+/// The trochoid fallback is tried only under Auto: its loops follow the
+/// medial line and have no ring order.
+pub(crate) fn adaptive_passes_from(center: &Region, p: &PocketParams, what: &str, stock: Option<&Region>, start: PassStart) -> Result<Planned, GenError> {
+    match start {
+        PassStart::Auto => adaptive_ordered(center, p, what, true, None, start),
+        PassStart::Outside => match stock.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
+            Some(st) => adaptive_ordered(center, p, what, false, Some(st), start),
+            None => rings(center, p, what, start, "has no stock outline to start from in the air"),
+        },
+        PassStart::Inside if center.loops().iter().any(|l| l.area() < 0.0) => {
+            rings(center, p, what, start, "cannot start on a hole wall without a full-width slot")
+        }
+        PassStart::Inside => adaptive_ordered(center, p, what, false, None, start),
+    }
+}
+
+/// Why the Trochoidal method refuses `start` (#3355), or `None`. Its
+/// loops follow the area's medial line and have no ring order, so Inside
+/// and Outside are refused by name, never ignored.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn trochoidal_pass_start_refusal(method: AdaptiveMethod, start: PassStart) -> Option<String> {
+    (method == AdaptiveMethod::Trochoidal && start != PassStart::Auto).then(|| {
+        format!(
+            "Pass starts at {} is not available with the Trochoidal method - its loops follow the medial line and have no ring order; use Auto or Spiral",
+            start.label()
+        )
+    })
+}
+
+/// The Offset rings in the order `start` asks, with the note that names
+/// the switch (an order is never changed in silence).
+fn rings(center: &Region, p: &PocketParams, what: &str, start: PassStart, why: &str) -> Result<Planned, GenError> {
+    let s = PocketStrategy::OffsetRings;
+    let step = crate::load::load_step(p.tool_diameter, p.optimal_load);
+    let note = format!(
+        "adaptive: Pass starts at {} - the HSM plan {why}{RINGS_FALLBACK}{what} in that order instead",
+        start.label()
+    );
+    Ok((plan_passes_from(center, step, p.climb, s, start)?, vec![note], s, None, Vec::new()))
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+#[path = "pocket_hsm_start_tests.rs"]
+mod tests;

+//! The ring and row plan of one planar area (split from `pocket.rs` for
+//! the 400-line law, #3316): the shape law both the 2-D pocket and the
+//! 3-D pocket's per-level plan share. Provenance: concentric offset rings
+//! and zigzag rows of published pocketing practice; no vendor material
+//! consulted.
+
+use crate::geo2d::{Point2, Region};
+
+use super::face::GenError;
+use super::pass_start::PassStart;
+use super::pocket_strategy::PocketStrategy;
+use super::pocket_zigzag::zigzag_passes;
+use super::waterscan::waterline_passes;
+
+/// Concentric rings marching inward: ring k is the cutter-center area
+/// eroded by `k * stepover`, travelled closed. Offsets are taken from
+/// `center` at absolute distances (never buffer-of-buffer), so micron
+/// quantization cannot compound across rings.
+/// The cutter-center passes for one planar area: the shape law both the
+/// 2-D pocket and the 3-D pocket's per-level plan share (the strategies
+/// band/erode `center` identically; only the numbers come from the
+/// operation's params either way).
+pub(crate) fn plan_passes(
+    center: &Region,
+    stepover: f64,
+    climb: bool,
+    strategy: PocketStrategy,
+) -> Result<Vec<Vec<Point2>>, GenError> {
+    plan_passes_from(center, stepover, climb, strategy, PassStart::Auto)
+}
+
+/// [`plan_passes`] with the side each level starts on (#3316): read by
+/// the ring tilings only; zigzag rows have no ring order.
+pub(crate) fn plan_passes_from(
+    center: &Region,
+    stepover: f64,
+    climb: bool,
+    strategy: PocketStrategy,
+    start: PassStart,
+) -> Result<Vec<Vec<Point2>>, GenError> {
+    match strategy {
+        PocketStrategy::Zigzag | PocketStrategy::Auto => zigzag_passes(center, stepover, climb),
+        // Offset rings are ring tiling at the caller's step; the HSM
+        // plan is `pocket_hsm.rs`'s (the planar pocket's own, and the
+        // 3-D ladder's per level through `machining3d::hsm`), which
+        // hands a refused area back here as rings.
+        PocketStrategy::Waterline | PocketStrategy::Adaptive | PocketStrategy::OffsetRings => {
+            waterline_passes(center, stepover, climb, start)
+        }
+    }
+}

+## #3316 - "Pass starts at" is one shared parameter (2D Offset first)
+
+**What was decided.**
+
+- One domain type, `machining2d::PassStart { Auto, Inside, Outside }`,
+  in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs`. `app` re-exports it.
+  Every kind with a pass order uses this type. No kind gets its own enum.
+- One project key, `pass_start` (`project::PassStartDto`, snake case).
+  `auto` is the default and is never written. Files without the key read
+  as Auto. There is no version step, and every file without a choice
+  stays byte-identical.
+- One command: the field is a plain `OpParams` field, so
+  `EditOperationParams` carries it (undo and redo included). One MCP
+  tool: the generic `edit_operation` merge patch. The patch guard keeps an
+  explicit `"auto"` (`pass_start_kept` in `mcp/edit.rs`), because a
+  skipped default never comes back from the round-trip.
+- One Passes-tab row, `Pass starts at`
+  (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pass_start_row.rs`). A kind shows the row when
+  its pane passes `Some(&mut pass_start)`.
+- The digest writes the value only off Auto, so every earlier operation
+  keeps its cache stamp.
+- The ring law (`PassStart::rank`), read by `waterline_passes`:
+  - Auto: the core first (`kmax - k`). This is the same stable sort as
+    the old `Reverse(k)`, so Auto is byte-identical.
+  - Outside: the loops of the outer boundary family (counter-clockwise)
+    from the boundary in, then the hole families (clockwise) from the core
+    back to their wall. On an Outside containment band the outer boundary
+    is the stock reach and the hole is the part, so the level starts with
+    the tool outside the stock and ends on the part wall. Each ring has
+    cut air on one side: no ring is a full slot.
+  - Inside: the mirror (holes from the wall out, then the outer family
+    from the core back).
+- Only 2D Offset reads it in this PR. The motion entry points are
+  `pocket_started` and `pocket_avoid_started`; the old
+  `pocket_entered_with_relief` and `pocket_avoid_with_relief` call them
+  with Auto. `plan_passes` calls `plan_passes_from` with Auto, so the 3-D
+  pocket, the HSM fallback and rest machining are not changed.
+
+**Room for the #1448 start point.** The start point (where on its ring a
+pass starts) and the exit point go beside `pass_start` as their own
+fields with their own key. The planner input is the pair: the ring rank
+chooses the order, the start point rotates each loop to its entry. The
+same entry functions take the new input when #1448 lands.
+
+**Why.** The maintainer asked for one parameter with one shape for every
+kind (#3316 comments, 2026-11-22). The field rides the existing command
+and MCP door, so the GUI and agents use the same undoable path.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- A `pass_start` field on `PocketParams`. About 57 struct literals
+  without `..` would change for one value that only one kind reads now.
+  An argument on the new entry functions keeps every other caller
+  byte-identical. When Pocket and Adaptive take the parameter (their
+  sub-issues), the field can move into `PocketParams` in one step.
+- A change of Auto for an Outside band. The maintainer said Auto keeps
+  the current behaviour.
+- A pure distance-from-boundary rank. It interleaves the two families
+  where the band width changes, and then a ring can have uncut stock on
+  both sides.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Low. The type and the key are shared already.
+A new kind adds its field, its row call and its planner read.

+## #3355 - "Pass starts at" on 2D Adaptive
+
+**What was decided.**
+
+- 2D Adaptive takes the shared `pass_start` field of #3316: the same
+  type (`machining2d::PassStart`), the same project key (`pass_start`,
+  `auto` never written), the same Passes-tab row and the same MCP door
+  (`edit_operation`). No new type. The digest writes the value only off
+  Auto, so every earlier operation keeps its cache stamp.
+- The law for the Spiral method (`pocket_hsm_start::adaptive_passes_from`):
+  - **Auto**: the plan every earlier file cut. The stock outline that
+    the generator now passes is not read. All goldens stay
+    byte-identical. A pin compares the two paths.
+  - **Outside**: each piece of the area is cut from the air past the
+    stock edge inward, with the #1950 air plan that the 3-D ladder
+    already uses. A piece that the air plan cannot start refuses the HSM
+    plan (`hsm_passes` with `air_only`), because the growth spiral would
+    start it in its core. Then the Offset rings cut the area in the
+    Outside order, at the load step. The note names the switch.
+  - **Inside**: in an area without holes, the growth plan is the Inside
+    order already. It starts at its bore in the core and grows out to
+    the wall, so the plan does not change. An area with holes (islands,
+    or the part of an Outside band) cannot start on a hole wall without
+    a full-width slot. The Offset rings cut it from the holes out. The
+    note names the switch.
+  - The trochoid fallback is tried only under Auto, because its loops
+    have no ring order. Every ring fallback takes the asked order.
+- The Trochoidal method refuses Inside and Outside by name: at the
+  command door (`named_refusal`), in the generator, and as a consequence
+  line under the row. This follows the pattern of corner relief and arc
+  turns under Trochoidal.
+- The stock outline goes to the planner only for an untilted operation,
+  because the outline is in world XY. A tilted Outside operation says
+  "no stock outline" and uses the Outside rings.
+
+**Why.** The maintainer asked for one parameter on every kind with a
+pass order (#3316, 2026-11-22). An adaptive plan keeps the tool load
+constant. It can start only in open air or in its own bore, never on a
+wall. So where the plan cannot honour the order, the rings honour it,
+and the note says so. The order is never dropped without a word.
+
+**Finding.** With an Outside containment, the 2D band stops where the
+tool's disc touches the stock (centre at stock edge + R). The air plan
+puts its entry ramp 0.005 mm (`AIR_GAP`) further out, outside the band.
+So on fig8 (the #2849 pin 3 case), Outside uses the Outside rings. The
+air plan runs where the boundary reaches farther past the stock (a
+sketch boundary bigger than the stock). A motion pin covers that path.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- A stock outline made smaller by the air gap, so that the fig8 band has
+  room for the air entry. The first plunge would then touch the stock.
+  That breaks the air plan's guarantee.
+- A band made wider past the stock for Outside. That changes the
+  containment law of every kind, and it is outside this issue.
+- A refusal of Outside where the air plan cannot start. The rings cut
+  the asked order with one stepover of engagement, so a refusal would
+  only take a working option from the user.
+- A "no pass order" row for 2D Adaptive. The Spiral method has an order
+  (growth from the bore, or air inward). Only Trochoidal has none, and
+  its row says so by name.
+
+**Room for #1448.** The start point and the exit point go beside
+`pass_start` as their own fields, as in the #3316 decision. The air plan
+and the rings each take an entry point. The growth plan already chooses
+its own bore (`choose_entry`).
+
+**Cost to change later.** Low. The law is one dispatch function. A
+wider Outside band would let the air plan cut fig8 with no change here.
